La pieza básica es el ruido de valor en: The basic piece is value noise in three dimensions. A number is drawn at each vertex of a grid of cubes, and inside each cube you interpolate: first along $x$ on the four edges, then along $y$ on the two faces, and lastly along $z$. Las texturas sólidas aparecieron dos vec: Solid textures appeared twice at the same conference: at SIGGRAPH 1985, Darwyn Peachey published Solid Texturing of Complex Surfaces and Ken Perlin An Image Synthesizer, where he presented his noise with examples of marble, fire and clouds. Perlin had started thinking about it after working on Tron (1982), fed up with the plastic look of computer images, and in 1997 he received a technical Oscar for the noise that bears his name.
Las texturas sólidas nacieron para el ci: Solid textures were born for the cinema, where a carved marble object has to be able to break and show coherent veins inside, and they are still in every render program as wood, marble or granite nodes. The games that generate whole planets do what this topic does, with more layers: noise for continents, rules by height and latitude, and clouds apart. Outside entertainment, the trilinear interpolation of eight corners is the one medical scanner viewers use to read between the voxels of a CT scan, and colour 3D printers use it to decide the colour of each drop of material inside the part.
